speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health in view of the target of 40,000 married couples between 2024 and 2027 against 674 screened at end 2025 under the regarding the PaREnthood genetic DIsease Carrier Test (PREDICT) Programme (a) what are the reasons for the low screening rate; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider including couples planning to get married, like those already on the HDB Fiancé/Fiancée Scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: These couples were then invited to undergo genetic counselling so that they understand how to interpret the results and potential implications.

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The first one, beyond awareness, what does the Ministry see as the key reasons why couples are not taking up PREDICT?

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Second, whether the Ministry has considered if earlier touchpoints, such as at the point of the Registry of Marriage or Registry of Muslim Marriages applications may be more effective in reaching couples?

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And if not, whether this is something the Ministry would consider?

speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Third, whether the Ministry has considered what role incentives could play in improving uptake?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Okay, the key reasons for not taking up.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Because this is a preconception test, KKH does not really come into contact with preconception couples.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, therefore, the only contact points they have are the fertility clinics and in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) clinics.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The couples there, I believe, just want to get pregnant.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, if you tell them about genetic tests and possible illnesses their child may have, I think they are probably not in the frame of mind to process the information.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And for many of them, I would think, love children and they will say, "Regardless of the situation, I am going to love the kid", and good for them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is just too much for couples to digest.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This programme was designed between the Temasek Foundation, the sponsor, and KKH.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: As the Member may know, I take a particular interest in genomics because I think it has the potential to transform and improve our healthcare system.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think the Ministry of Health (MOH) will want to dive into this PREDICT programme.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Members might be aware of some of the protocols that we have set up – one for familial hypercholesterolemia (FH), and recently, for BReast CAncer genes (BRCA) 1 and 2 – and there are certain principles that we adopt when we implement genomics in healthcare.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And that will provide the assurance to many couples.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But to lump 80 diseases into one test, I think, it may be too much.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, MOH will take an interest in this.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will study how to implement this better because I think there is great potential for us to improve this.
